rationale: Evidence from iteration 6 (score 255.7, best so far): base_speed 1.3 on the iteration 5 design gave 9 of 20 oval finishes (up from 2 of 20), line_loss_events 0 on all tracks, oval mean finish time 1.89 s, and oval max_error down to 0.0535 m (from 0.060). Speed did not cause the drift; it helped finishes. The approved review for this iteration sets the next test: with line loss at 0 and finishes held, keep base_speed 1.3 and move only the sensor row toward the axle. Max_error has sat at 0.060 to 0.064 m in every earlier design, and sensors at y = 0.03 m sit 3 cm ahead of the axle, so lag is a plausible cause. Change: sensor_positions y from 0.03 to 0.01 m for all seven sensors. x positions, weights, base_speed 1.3, kp 5.0, ki 0.02, kd 0.8 and last_direction are unchanged, so this race isolates the row move against the 255.7 baseline. Expected result: max_error below about 0.055 m on the s-bend and slalom, with oval finishes at or above 9 of 20 and no line-loss events. Risks: the row is closer to the axle, so the sensor-to-line reading may change more abruptly on sharp bends, which could add oscillation, and the slalom still logged about one line-loss event per run in iteration 5. Hypotheses: (a) max_error is lag-limited by sensors placed far ahead of the axle; (b) the y move alone reduces off-track exits without touching finishes. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion time, rms and max error, line-loss events, steering oscillation, control effort, controller errors and noise robustness. If finishes drop to 0 with line loss still 0, revert to y = 0.03 m and test base_speed 1.2 alone. If steering oscillation exceeds about 0.4 while max_error is below 0.05 m, lower kd to about 0.5.
